For thermal loads, the differential must be large enough to make up for losses, and therefore the Mild tariff does not drive quite as much load response as the Medium and Full tariffs. This is best captured by the effective shed results (Figure 20), which show technical potential of 5.5 GW for Full tariff (2030 low price scenario), 5.4 GW for Medium, and about 4.8 GW for Mild, with most of the difference coming from a reduction in residential cooling load response. While the load response is similar across the tariff designs, the bill impacts are substantially different. The Medium and Mild tariffs offer aggregate customer bill savings that are about 70% and 25% the savings possible on the Full tariff, respectively (Figure 22). Despite the reduced bill savings, we find that the total economic potential (both “cost effective” and “short payback” thresholds) is still quite substantial across all tariff designs. With the expected widespread development and adoption of low-cost end use communications and control capabilities, even the Mild tariff offers enough savings to pay back 4 GW of effective shed potential in a 3-year payback period (Figure 29). The impact of tariff design does vary significantly across end uses, however. EV chargers are expected to be largely connected by 2030, so even Mild tariff price differentials are enough to drive complete load shifting (in our load response model) that is completely cost effective from the customer perspective. However, our model does not capture behavioral considerations around customer preferences and conveniences, that may mean they are less willing to shift load for small savings than they would be for larger savings. Our results only hold true in a world where load response is automated, passive, and does not impact the customer’s service level. Diversions from this simplified world are discussed in Section 4.3. The end use that is most affected by price design is space cooling, and particularly commercial space cooling. As Figure 29 shows, Medium and Full tariffs both offer about 2.5 GW of shed potential from space cooling, with about 1 GW coming from commercial and 1.5 GW from residential sectors. On the Medium tariff design, the technical potential is nearly identical to the Full tariff, but the “short payback” potential is somewhat limited in the commercial sector, dropping the effective shed to 0.6 GW. On the Mild tariff design, we see a reduction both in the technical potential of these loads (0.7 GW from commercial and 1.1 GW from residential), and a substantial decrease in the short payback period of commercial cooling; only 0.2 GW of effective shed appears.
